meta.notes: One mutant per enforcement mechanism, and for F3 one per EVASION SHAPE the brief names. EVERY SEARCH ANCHOR IS A SINGLE LINE: the working tree is CRLF here (git core.autocrlf normalizes on commit), and a multi-line pattern spelled with \n silently matches NOTHING against CRLF - the wave-12 trap the applier exists to refuse. Single-line anchors are convention-independent, and each is asserted unique by the applier. Inserted lines in replacements use \n; the compiler is indifferent and the restore is byte-exact from the in-memory copy. Every mutant COMPILES (verified by an in-memory-restored `go build ./...` + `go vet` probe before this spec was committed), so no kill is a disguised compile error. W16M2 and W16M8 are killed by DB-backed tests: the loop environment must export TEST_DATABASE_URL (the wave scratch DB solvent_t9w16) and SOLVENT_DATABASE_URL (the live DSN the destructive-split guard compares against). W16M2's kill is specifically an observation made DURING the cleanup - the mutant's post-return state is indistinguishable from the fix's (gate open, connection closed), which is exactly why round 14 found the bug by reading defer order rather than by running the old test.
